class.name: LensFlare3D
class.brief_description: A source of lens flare, drawn in screen space wherever the camera can see it.
class.description: A [LensFlare3D] marks a point in the world bright enough to scatter inside a camera lens: the sun, a headlamp, a window catching the light. The [member flare] resource says what that scattering looks like, and this node says where the source is, how bright it is, and when it should fade out. The flare is drawn into the HDR colour buffer before glow and tonemapping, so it blooms and is exposed along with the rest of the frame rather than being painted over the finished image. Which cameras pick a flare up is the camera's decision. [Camera3D] compares its [member Camera3D.lens_flare_cull_mask] against this node's [member VisualInstance3D.layers], separately from [member Camera3D.cull_mask], so a flare can be hidden from one camera without hiding whatever is throwing it. With no [member flare] of its own the node draws the engine's default flare, so one dropped into a scene shows something straight away. Assign a [LensFlare] to replace it; [method LensFlare.create_default] returns a copy of that same default to edit. [b]Note:[/b] Lens flares are only drawn by the Forward+ and Mobile renderers. The Compatibility renderer ignores them.

method.name: add_occlusion_exception
method.description: Makes the flare look past [param node] when it checks whether its source is hidden. The source is hidden by anything in front of it, so a flare inside a bulb is hidden by the bulb's own glass; add the bulb's mesh and it isn't, while a wall or a hand between the lamp and the camera still hides it. [codeblock] # The flare is a child of the bulb's mesh. $Bulb/Flare.add_occlusion_exception($Bulb) [/codeblock] It works on anything visible: a [MeshInstance3D], its children, a [MultiMeshInstance3D], CSG shapes, particles. An excluded object is looked past where it is, using its world-space bounds, so it follows the object when it moves. Up to 8 objects count per flare. Adding a node twice does nothing. [b]Note:[/b] Bounds are boxes. A surface that lies inside an excluded object's box is treated as the object, so a wall pressed right up against an excluded lamp is looked past where it is inside the lamp's box and hides the flare everywhere else.

method.name: clear_occlusion_exceptions
method.description: Removes every exception, so everything in front of the source hides it again.

method.name: get_occlusion_exception_nodes
method.description: Returns the nodes the flare looks past, however they were added. Nodes that have been freed, or that a path no longer leads to, are left out.

method.name: remove_occlusion_exception
method.description: Makes [param node] hide the source again, if it was added with [method add_occlusion_exception] or in [member occlusion_exceptions].

members.member: Paths, from this node, to the [VisualInstance3D]s the flare looks past when it checks whether its source is hidden. Put a flare in a bulb and add the bulb here, so its glass doesn't hide it. See [method add_occlusion_exception]. Saved with the scene.

How softly the flare fades out as the camera leaves the cone set by [member angle_limit], as a fraction of the cone. [code]0.0[/code] cuts the flare off at the edge of the cone. Has no effect when [member angle_limit] is [code]0.0[/code] or [member directional] is [code]true[/code].

Half-angle of a cone around the node's local -Z axis, outside of which the flare is not drawn. Use it for a source that only throws a flare when you are looking into it, such as a headlamp or a spotlight. [code]0.0[/code] disables the limit and the flare is drawn from every direction. Has no effect when [member directional] is [code]true[/code].
The colour of the source. Elements with [member LensFlareElement.tint_by_source] enabled are multiplied by it, which is how one flare resource can serve lights of different colours.

If [code]true[/code], the source is treated as infinitely far away and only the node's rotation matters, the way a [DirectionalLight3D] works. The source lies along the node's local +Z axis, so pointing the node the same way as a [DirectionalLight3D] puts the flare on that light. While this is enabled the flare cannot be occluded by distance or angle, so [member fade_distance_begin], [member fade_distance_end], [member angle_limit] and [member angle_fade] are ignored.
Distance from the camera at which the flare starts fading out. Fading is disabled unless [member fade_distance_end] is greater than this. Ignored when [member directional] is [code]true[/code].
Distance from the camera at which the flare has faded out completely. Ignored when [member directional] is [code]true[/code].

How far past the edge of the screen the source keeps throwing a flare, as a fraction of the screen. Larger values let a flare linger as the source leaves the frame instead of snapping off; [code]0.0[/code] cuts it at the edge.
The elements this source draws. Left empty, the node draws the engine's default flare instead of nothing.
Multiplies the size of every element, so a whole flare can be resized without editing the resource.
Multiplies the brightness of every element. Values above [code]1.0[/code] push the flare into the range where glow picks it up.

Angular radius of the disc sampled against the depth buffer, used instead of [member occlusion_radius] when [member directional] is [code]true[/code], because a source at infinity has no size in metres. The sun is about half a degree across; the default of one degree fades a little more softly than that. Keep it small. A wide angle samples a disc larger than most things that could block the source, so the flare goes on showing through them.

If [code]true[/code], the flare is faded out by whatever the scene drew in front of the source, sampled from the depth buffer over a disc of [member occlusion_radius] (or [member occlusion_angle] for a directional source). Partially hidden sources give a partially faded flare rather than an all-or-nothing pop. Samples that fall outside the frame are clamped to the nearest edge of the depth buffer, so a source just off screen is still occluded by whatever fills the edge of the view.

Radius of the disc sampled against the depth buffer, in metres at the source. A larger radius makes the flare fade earlier and more gradually as something moves in front of it. Replaced by [member occlusion_angle] when [member directional] is [code]true[/code].
